goal: Is ke baad aap menus aur input validation ke liye do-while loop likh sakenge, samjha sakenge ke woh kam az kam ek dafa kyun run hota hai, aur for, while aur do-while mein se choose kar sakenge.
warmup: Restaurant mein waiter ko aap ke faisla karne se pehle menu lana hota hai. Woh pehle yeh nahi puch sakta 'Kya aap ne decide kar liya?' kyunke aap ne abhi dishes dekhi hi nahi. Pehle woh action karta hai (menu dikhata hai), aur uske baad check karta hai ke aap order dena chahte hain ya nahi. ATM bhi aise hi kaam karta hai: woh pehle aap se PIN maangta hai, aur aap ke type karne ke baad hi check kar sakta hai ke woh sahi hai ya nahi. Agar ghalat ho to woh dobara poochta hai. 'Pehle karo, baad mein check karo' hi do-while loop hai.
definition: Do-while loop pehle apni body run karta hai aur har round ke baad condition check karta hai. Is wajah se body hamesha kam az kam ek dafa run hoti hai. Isey post-test (exit-controlled) loop kehte hain. Yeh C++ ka akela loop hai jo semicolon par khatam hota hai: do { ... } while (condition);
howItWorks: Isey while se compare karein. While mein check upar hota hai, do-while mein neeche. Pipeline chalayein: body, phir condition. Agar condition true ho to loop dobara ghoomta hai, warna khatam ho jata hai. Classic saboot: int i = 10; do { cout << i; } while (i < 5); 10 print karta hai, haalanke 10 < 5 false hai, kyunke test se pehle body ek dafa run ho chuki thi. Isi condition wala while loop kuch bhi print nahi karta. Hum isey kahan use karte hain? (1) Menus: menu dikhayein, choice parhein, aur tab tak dohrayein jab tak user Exit na chune. (2) Input validation: koi value maangein, aur jab tak value invalid ho sawal dohrate rahein. Aakhri while (...) ke baad semicolon yaad rakhein. Neeche wali table ka aakhri hissa teeno loops ko compare karta hai.
